title: A broadly protective HIV vaccine

concept.text: Concept synthesis: A broadly protective HIV vaccine would train the immune system to prevent acquisition of genetically diverse HIV strains and sustain that protection across diverse people. The intended advance is durable prevention of infection, rather than an immune response that recognizes only the vaccine strain. Breadth across strains, durability over time and consistent protection across populations are distinct requirements.

Scientific framing from the supplied research: HIV’s diversity, rapid evolution and shielding of vulnerable sites make broad protection difficult. One proposed route is germline targeting: initiating responses in precursor immune cells capable of developing into cells that produce broadly neutralizing antibodies. Activating those precursors is an intermediate step; the complete innovation requires the resulting immune response to prevent HIV acquisition. The supplied retained scientific source could not substantiate the mechanism or reported experimental findings, so this framing remains an explanatory synthesis of the inputs.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: Durable protection against diverse circulating HIV strains could substantially reduce dependence on continuing preventive medication and repeated access to prevention services. Its practical value would depend on the degree and duration of protection, the number of doses, any booster requirements and whether people can readily obtain the vaccine. A demanding vaccination schedule could retain substantial dependence on continuing services.

Conditional public-health synthesis: Broad individual protection could contribute to reducing transmission, but elimination would also depend on vaccine coverage, effective delivery, treatment and other prevention measures. Protection demonstrated in a trial would not by itself establish elimination at population scale. The revolutionary potential lies in adding durable, broadly applicable prevention; neither the magnitude of that benefit nor elimination of transmission is established by the supplied evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: Scientific synthesis: The missing capability is to induce an immune response that reliably prevents acquisition across HIV’s genetic diversity, remains protective over time and works across diverse recipients. The barriers identified in the research—viral diversity, evolution and shielding of vulnerable sites—mean that recognizing a selected vaccine antigen is an insufficient endpoint. The response must reach vulnerable features shared broadly enough among circulating viruses to support meaningful protection. These mechanisms are stated in the research but lack inspectable scientific support in the supplied retained source.

Engineering synthesis: For the germline-targeting route described in the inputs, precursor activation must lead to a sufficiently broad and durable protective response. The reported neutralization by a subset of isolated antibodies, even if confirmed, would leave unresolved whether vaccination produces adequate protection in recipients. Antibody precursor activation, neutralization measured with isolated antibodies and prevention of human infection are different achievements; success at one does not establish the others.

Practical synthesis: A successful product would also need acceptable safety and a vaccination schedule feasible for broad delivery. Durability, booster burden, viral escape and performance across populations must be addressed together. A biologically promising response would remain an incomplete solution if its protection waned quickly or its delivery requirements prevented widespread use.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes a phase 1 germline-targeting result to Caniels and colleagues, “Precise targeting of HIV broadly neutralizing antibody precursors in humans,” listed as published in Science on 31 July 2025, DOI 10.1126/science.adv5572. It reports activation of desired broadly neutralizing antibody precursor cells in most recipients and neutralization by a subset of isolated antibodies. These are reported findings whose bibliographic identity, date and scientific content could not be independently confirmed from the retained material described in the review.

The earlier description that an abstract had been assessed requires correction. According to the supplied review, the retained copy contained only a cookie-access notice, with no inspectable abstract or trial results. It therefore does not verify recipient proportions, the extent of neutralization or the purported paper’s identity. The source index records a saved artifact, but successful saving does not establish that scientific content was accessible. This access and extraction limitation is not evidence that the reported findings are false.

Interpretive synthesis: If confirmed, the reported phase 1 findings would represent an immunological step toward a vaccine, not demonstrated protection against HIV acquisition. The supplied research gives no exact recipient fraction beyond “most,” no quantitative neutralization breadth or potency, and no duration of protection. Those quantities cannot be reconstructed from the retained copy. No vaccine efficacy result can be established from the supplied material.

Evidence-scope limitation: The supplied freshness record is empty, so the inputs do not establish the latest development status or whether this remained an open breakthrough as of 1 November 2026. The source index’s retrieval timestamp of 11 November 2026 does not resolve that gap because the retained content did not expose the scientific document. The dated study report should therefore be preserved with its limitations rather than presented as a verified current frontier.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Randomized trials across populations and regions should show protection against HIV acquisition under exposure to genetically diverse circulating strains, with acceptable safety and a vaccination schedule feasible for broad delivery. Acquisition should be the decisive clinical endpoint; precursor activation and antibody neutralization would help explain the response but would not substitute for demonstrated protection.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized trials demonstrate protection against acquisition of diverse HIV strains

completion_criteria.text: Proposed operational criteria: Before judging completion, investigators would need to specify the required magnitude of protection, the duration of follow-up and how viral diversity and population coverage will be assessed. The supplied inputs establish no numerical efficacy target, minimum duration or accepted breadth threshold. Such thresholds would be proposed evaluation choices, not established standards. Finite trials could demonstrate protection over the strains, populations and periods studied, without proving protection against every possible HIV variant or in every person.
completion_criteria.label: Protection thresholds and evaluation scope are specified before judging completion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed confirmation and practical boundaries: Convincing evidence would include reproducible protection across independent trials or settings, follow-up for waning and viral escape, and evaluation of effectiveness outside trials. Delivery studies should establish whether the dose schedule, booster requirements and access burden support broad use. Conclusions should state the demonstrated duration, populations and exposure settings rather than extending trial findings beyond their measured scope.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible protection is confirmed and practical limits are established

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: INF-02, “A safe, scalable cure for established HIV infection,” concerns the same virus but a different endpoint: resolving infection that already exists. INF-01 concerns preventing acquisition. INF-11, “A safe, broadly effective treatment-free cure for chronic hepatitis B,” likewise concerns established infection and freedom from continuing treatment. These cure concepts share interests in durable benefit and reduced medication burden, while remaining separate from preventive HIV vaccination.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-08, “A pre-emptive vaccine against diverse pandemic coronaviruses,” is closely related through the aim of protection across viral diversity. INF-09, “A rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen,” instead centers on response speed and the development-to-delivery process. INF-03, “A tuberculosis vaccine that interrupts transmission,” and INF-13, “A highly protective, durable and readily deliverable malaria vaccine,” overlap in vaccine performance and delivery goals; INF-03 explicitly emphasizes transmission interruption, whereas INF-01’s primary proposed endpoint is prevention of HIV acquisition.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-04, “A reliable way to break malaria transmission through its vectors,” shares the population goal of reducing transmission but targets vectors. INF-10, “Prevention of multiple sclerosis by controlling Epstein–Barr virus,” and INF-14, “Mechanism-guided prevention of major post-viral syndromes,” concern preventing downstream disease associated with viral infection. Their endpoints differ from INF-01’s direct prevention of acquisition, even where control of infection could contribute to both.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” concerns diagnosis and treatment selection. INF-06, “A dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments,” INF-07, “Broad-spectrum treatment for unrelated viral infections,” INF-12, “Very short, reliable curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis,” and INF-15, “A rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform,” concern treatment capabilities. Their overlap with INF-01 is the wider aim of controlling infectious disease; their diagnostic or therapeutic endpoints do not establish vaccine-induced prevention.

unresolved_issues: The purported paper’s identity, publication details and reported phase 1 findings require confirmation from accessible scientific content.
Exact recipient proportions, neutralization breadth and potency, assay scope and response durability are not established by the supplied material.
The stated biological barriers and germline-targeting rationale lack inspectable supporting scientific text in this evidence package.
The latest development status, including continued openness as of 1 November 2026, cannot be established from the empty freshness record.
Operational efficacy, durability, strain-diversity and population-coverage thresholds remain to be defined; the proposed completion criteria are not documented consensus standards.

brief.title: Lasting protection against many forms of HIV
possible: People could be vaccinated against many genetically different forms of HIV and stay protected over time. The vaccine would prevent infection across diverse people, rather than train the immune system to recognize only the form used in the vaccine.
why: For people at risk of HIV, lasting protection could reduce dependence on continuing preventive medication and repeated visits to prevention services.
Broad protection could also reduce transmission, adding another way for communities to prevent new infections.

sources.showed: An early human trial reportedly activated immune cells capable of developing into producers of antibodies, proteins that block viruses. Some isolated antibodies blocked HIV.
sources.cited_for: The study supports an early step toward training the immune system to block many forms of HIV.
sources.not_established: Activating these cells does not establish that vaccination prevents infection or produces lasting, broad protection.

sources.who: Supachai Rerks-Ngarm and the MOPH–TAVEG investigators
sources.showed: A randomized trial in Thailand found modest protection against HIV infection in an analysis excluding people already infected when the trial began. Other analyses were inconclusive.
sources.quote:
there was a trend toward 
the prevention of HIV-1 infection among the vaccine recipients
sources.cited_for: The trial provides human evidence that vaccination can reduce the risk of acquiring HIV.
sources.not_established: The trial did not establish durable protection across diverse strains and populations.

sources.showed: Vaccination induced families of antibody-producing immune cells in humans. Their strongest antibodies blocked some HIV strains beyond those targeted by the vaccine.
sources.quote: Neutralization was enhanced by vaccine selection of improbable mutations that increased antibody binding to gp41 and lipids.
sources.cited_for: The study shows that vaccination can start antibody responses that block different HIV strains.
sources.not_established: Blocking viruses with isolated antibodies does not establish that vaccinated people are protected from infection.

sources.who: Jordan R Willis, Madhu Prabhakaran, Michelle Muthui and colleagues
sources.showed: A follow-up vaccine dose advanced the development of immune cells toward producing antibodies that block many HIV strains. Initial activation of these cells was also demonstrated in Africa.
sources.cited_for: The work supports guiding an initial immune response further toward broad virus blocking.
sources.not_established: Early development of the desired immune cells does not establish broad or lasting prevention of HIV infection.

shown: Rerks-Ngarm and colleagues found modest protection in a randomized trial in Thailand: an estimated 31.2% reduction in infection risk after excluding participants already infected at the start. Other analyses were inconclusive.

Williams and colleagues induced antibodies that blocked some different HIV strains in laboratory tests. That advances the immune response, but does not show that those vaccinated were protected from infection.
missing: Trials have yet to establish reliable prevention of infection across genetically diverse HIV strains and diverse recipients.
Protection has yet to be shown to last while resisting changes in the virus that let it evade the immune response.
A broadly protective vaccine still needs acceptable safety and a dose schedule that people can readily complete.

milestones.label: Trials demonstrate protection across diverse HIV strains
milestones.explanation: Randomized trials would have to show safe prevention of HIV infection across populations and regions with a feasible vaccination schedule. Preventing infection is the decisive test of protection.

milestones.label: Criteria for judging protection are defined in advance
milestones.explanation: Investigators would have to define the required protection, follow-up period, strain diversity and population coverage before judging success. These criteria would make clear what counts as broad, lasting protection.

milestones.label: Protection is reproduced and practical limits are established
milestones.explanation: Independent trials and everyday use would have to confirm protection, track fading protection and virus escape, and assess delivery demands. This would establish how reliably and widely the vaccine could work.

uncertain: It remains unclear whether activating the desired immune cells can lead to antibodies that prevent infection across many HIV strains.
The required strength, duration and breadth of protection have no agreed thresholds in this proposed test of success.
The number of doses and need for boosters could determine how much the vaccine reduces dependence on continuing prevention services.

page.title: Cross-clade HIV-1 vaccine
page.definition: A preventive vaccine reduces HIV-1 acquisition across clades, the virus’s major genetic subdivisions, and across recipient populations. Protection persists during clinical follow-up and is demonstrated through infection endpoints in people.

goal.need: Global annual HIV acquisitions declined by 42% between 2010 and 2025, but prevention has not stopped acquisition. In 2025, 78% of people living with HIV were receiving antiretroviral treatment. The remaining acquisitions and continuing treatment burden establish the scale of the prevention problem.

figures.caption: Global HIV burden in 2025
figures.note: UNAIDS estimates cover all HIV types. Ranges are those reported by UNAIDS.

statements.body: International AIDS Society, Global HIV Vaccine Enterprise
statements.quote: A safe and effective HIV vaccine that is available to the world.
statements.context: The vision stated in the Enterprise’s Strategic Plan 2022–2027.

statements.quote: Scientists widely believe that a vaccine inducing broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) could provide broad protection against many strains of HIV.
statements.context: IAVI states the rationale for its sequential vaccination strategy. Broadly neutralizing antibodies block multiple HIV strains.

completion.title: One HIV-1 vaccine regimen demonstrates protection across clades and populations in human efficacy trials.
completion.criterion: The same vaccine regimen demonstrates a reduction in laboratory-confirmed HIV-1 acquisition over 3 years, with the lower bound of its 95% confidence interval above 30%, in randomized controlled efficacy studies covering different circulating clades and recipient populations. Safety findings support use in those populations. The clinical benchmark comes from a NIAID-convened workshop; requiring its demonstration across clades and populations is an Atlas operational extension.
completion.set_by: Atlas operational test extending the NIAID-convened workshop’s clinical efficacy benchmark to cross-clade protection.
completion.basis: Searches of WHO product profiles, FDA vaccine approval guidance, the IAS vaccine roadmap, HVTN protocols and NIAID workshop reports found no combined completion rule for efficacy, strain breadth, duration and population coverage. AVAC identifies the absence of an updated field-wide product profile. The workshop provides an attributable clinical benchmark, but its extension across clades and populations is an Atlas choice.

milestones.title: An HIV-1 vaccine activates broadly neutralizing antibody precursor B cells in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: Vaccination activates the intended antibody precursor B cells and produces class-compatible memory responses in an experimental animal model. Jardine and colleagues demonstrated VRC01-class priming in engineered mice in 2015, using five mice per immunization group for B-cell sorting or antibody-binding assays. A later study published on 30 June 2026 used 24 rhesus macaques; serum broadly neutralizing activity was demonstrated in eight of the 18 animals receiving heterologous boosting. These are immune-response results, not demonstrations of human protection.
milestones.set_by: Community convention of peer-reviewed mechanistic proof of concept, applied by Jardine and colleagues; precursor engagement is also recognized in the NIAID/DAIDS development framework.
milestones.threshold_quote: The results suggest that rational epitope design can prime rare B cell precursors for affinity maturation to desired targets.

milestones.title: An HIV-1 vaccine activates the intended antibody precursor B cells in a human phase 1 trial.
milestones.criterion: A human phase 1 study demonstrates vaccine-induced engagement of the intended broadly neutralizing antibody precursor B cells while assessing safety and tolerability. In IAVI C101, 47 adults received GT1.1 vaccine or placebo: 20 received 30 μg, 19 received 300 μg and eight received placebo. Caniels and colleagues reported VRC01-class precursor induction in most vaccine recipients in the paper published on 31 July 2025. The publication does not establish prevention of HIV acquisition.
milestones.set_by: NIAID Division of AIDS, published framework for selecting immunologic endpoints for HIV vaccine advancement.
milestones.threshold_quote: engagement of the intended naïve B-cell precursors

milestones.title: A different booster advances vaccine-primed antibody lineages toward broadly neutralizing antibodies in people.
milestones.criterion: After priming, a heterologous booster advances the same antibody lineages through maturation, assessed through mutation, antigen-binding affinity and neutralization measurements. The IAVI G002 study enrolled 60 adults in the United States; IAVI G003 enrolled 18 in Rwanda and South Africa. The paper published on 31 July 2025 demonstrated increased mutation, affinity and neutralization activity after heterologous boosting in G002. Skin reactions occurred in 18% of G002 participants. These studies evaluated safety and immune responses, not acquisition efficacy.
milestones.set_by: NIAID Division of AIDS, published framework for sequential HIV vaccine development.
milestones.threshold_quote: progression of those lineages through sequential boosting

milestones.title: Vaccination induces human antibodies that neutralize heterologous tier 2 HIV-1 viruses.
milestones.criterion: Antibodies derived from vaccinated people neutralize heterologous tier 2 viruses: strains absent from the vaccine and having neutralization resistance typical of circulating HIV-1. HVTN 133 planned 20 vaccine and four placebo recipients; its strongest isolated antibody lineage neutralized 15% of the global tier 2 panel and 35% of clade B strains. On 26 March 2026, Sanders reported an isolated antibody neutralizing 56% of 119 viruses after C107/C110 boosting: 12 participants enrolled and ten received both vaccinations. That conference result was not peer reviewed. Neither result establishes protective serum levels.
milestones.set_by: HVTN 133 registered protocol, exploratory objective 2, explicitly includes tier 2 neutralization by isolated monoclonal antibodies; the protocol concerns an MPER peptide-liposome vaccine.
milestones.threshold_quote: neutralization including tier 2 virus bnAb activity

milestones.title: An HIV-1 vaccine reduces acquisition in a randomized trial at its prespecified significance threshold.
milestones.criterion: A randomized efficacy study demonstrates reduced laboratory-confirmed HIV-1 acquisition under its prespecified analysis and statistical success rule. RV144 randomized 16,402 adults in Thailand. Its modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded seven participants infected at baseline and estimated 31.2% efficacy over 42 months: 95% confidence interval 1.1–52.1%; P = 0.04. The intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses were inconclusive. This establishes a clinical signal in that setting, without establishing cross-clade protection.
milestones.set_by: RV144 investigators, prespecified final statistical analysis plan described in the trial publication.
milestones.threshold_quote: A P value of less than 0.05 was considered to indicate statistical significance.

milestones.title: An HIV-1 vaccine shows acquisition efficacy above 30% at 95% confidence over 3 years.
milestones.criterion: An efficacy study demonstrates reduced HIV-1 acquisition over 3 years with a lower 95% confidence bound above 30%, alongside safety evidence supporting the intended use. A NIAID-convened workshop treated this degree of acquisition protection as sufficient to support licensure in its hypothetical trial scenarios. This is the workshop’s benchmark, not a binding FDA rule. RV144 did not meet it: the lower confidence bound in its modified intention-to-treat analysis was 1.1%. Demonstrating this result across clades and populations remains the completion test.
milestones.set_by: Expert panel at the NIAID Division of AIDS workshop on HIV vaccine endpoints and regulatory issues, published in 2007.
milestones.threshold_quote: trial scenarios that statistically demonstrated reduction in infection rates of at least 30% over a 3-year period were deemed sufficient to support licensure

not_found: No field-wide minimum number of clades or recipient populations defining a broadly protective HIV vaccine was located.
The 2015 HVTN target-product-profile slide deck could not be fetched.
PMC full texts for the supplied Caniels, Willis and Williams studies returned access checks; accessible abstracts and institutional materials were used.
